title: False Wake
summary: On the night shift, a half-deaf annotator who labels accidental smart-speaker recordings gets a clip from her own locked kitchen in which her dead brother's voice says her name.

fields.synopsis: In Dayton in 2029, Nell Varga works nights in a gutted department store, labelling the four-second clips that Hearth smart speakers send home when they wake by mistake. Most of what she hears is houses where no one is talking. At 3:09 one morning a clip comes up from her own kitchen: her old fridge, her broken Goodwill clock, and the voice of her brother Danny, who drowned in February, saying "Nellie?" Her app shows a feature called Company that she never turned on, enabled by Halden the day she came home from his funeral. Her remote supervisor, Paul, tells her to label the clip no speech detected. Instead she listens in on her empty apartment live and hears someone fill her kettle, sit down at her table and say she never listened to Danny's last voicemail. Then the session is ended by someone in her home.

generator.cover_prompt: Grainy risograph-style illustration with hard shadows and flat layered inks, in sodium-vapor amber, deep slate blue, bone white and signal red. A narrow old apartment kitchen at night, seen from the dark doorway: a dented enamel kettle on a small blue gas flame, a wooden chair pulled out from a bare kitchen table as if someone just sat down, a starburst wall clock with no numerals, and high above the cabinets a small cylindrical smart speaker glowing with one faint light. No people. Amber light from a streetlamp spills through the window across the linoleum; deep slate shadows fill the corners. The composition is wide and low with generous empty space around the chair. The mood is quietly ominous and intimate.
